classification.classification_note: The saved ASan witness is an invalid-free in `xmlFreeNodeList` during `xmlParseBalancedChunkMemoryInternal` cleanup, reached while the schema parser is reading attacker-controlled XML. ASan reports that the freed address lies inside a dictionary allocation made by `xmlDictAddString`/`xmlDictLookup`, so cleanup frees a non-malloc base. The patch shows the intended caller-side guard in `xmlParseReference`, but the staged source-grounded trace here is limited to the balanced-chunk cleanup path that is directly supported by the saved sanitizer stack and local source.

bug_description.original: An invalid-free in libxml2's parser (parser.c) causes xmlFreeNodeList/xmlFreeNode to attempt to free an address that was not obtained from malloc. The error occurs during reference/balanced-chunk parsing (xmlParseReference / xmlParseBalancedChunkMemoryInternal), leading to crashes and potential heap corruption when processing crafted XML (e.g., schema) inputs.

bug_description.normalized: The saved witness is an OSS-Fuzz schema testcase. The harness builds a schema parser context whose dictionary is created in `xmlSchemaNewParserCtxt`, then `xmlSchemaAddSchemaDoc` calls `xmlCtxtReadFile` and regular XML parsing reaches `xmlParseReference`. The ASan trace shows that this path invokes `xmlParseBalancedChunkMemoryInternal`, whose cleanup always frees `ctxt->myDoc->children` after the nested balanced-chunk parse. Recursive destruction reaches `DICT_FREE(cur->name)` in `xmlFreeNodeList`, and ASan reports the freed address is 92 bytes inside a 1048-byte region allocated by `xmlDictAddString`/`xmlDictLookup`, meaning a dictionary-owned interior pointer is passed to `free`. The fix commit adds an early `if (!ctxt->wellFormed) return;` in `xmlParseReference`, but the staged vulnerable source available in this session already contains that guard, so this Stage 02 package does not claim a caller-state continuation mechanism beyond the source-supported schema/entity-reference path evidenced by the sanitizer stack.

source.description: First project-code statement on the witnessed crashing path that consumes attacker-controlled entity-reference syntax and materializes the entity object later reparsed as a balanced chunk.
source.value_from: The fuzz harness is only the unscored boundary. The testcase is admitted as a schema document by `xmlSchemaAddSchemaDoc`, and regular XML parsing reaches `xmlParseReference`, where `xmlParseEntityRef(ctxt)` parses attacker-controlled markup into `ent`.

relation.description: The entity pointer assigned to `ent` comes directly from parsing the attacker-controlled entity reference.

root_cause.description: Balanced-chunk teardown frees the temporary pseudo-root tree even on the failing path evidenced by ASan; recursive cleanup later reaches a node name pointer that is not safe to free as a malloc base address.
root_cause.note: This is the latest project statement before the reported bad-free that creates the vulnerable cleanup state seen in the sanitizer trace. The saved runtime evidence and local source support that `xmlParseBalancedChunkMemoryInternal` tears down `ctxt->myDoc->children` unconditionally after the nested parse, but do not source-groundedly disambiguate an earlier caller-side predicate in the staged tree because local `xmlParseReference` already contains the patched `if (!ctxt->wellFormed) return;` guard.

parser_admitted.description: The schema parser admits the testcase as a schema document and hands its bytes to the regular XML parser.

fine_trace.note: Source. The attacker-controlled entity reference is parsed into `ent`, the entity object used by the later balanced-chunk parse shown in the sanitizer stack.
The resolved entity is treated as an internal general entity, selecting the branch that reparses replacement text as a balanced chunk.
`xmlParseReference` reparses the selected entity replacement text `ent->content` as a nested balanced chunk.
The nested parser installs a temporary `pseudoroot` under `ctxt->myDoc->children`, creating the tree that later cleanup will free.

Root-cause step. After the nested parse, teardown frees the temporary pseudo-root tree rooted at `ctxt->myDoc->children`; the ASan stack shows this cleanup call immediately above `xmlFreeNodeList`/`xmlFreeNode`.

Sink. Recursive teardown reaches `DICT_FREE(cur->name)`, and ASan shows the freed pointer is 92 bytes inside the dictionary region allocated by `xmlDictAddString`/`xmlDictLookup`, so cleanup attempts to free a non-malloc base address.

allocation_context.summary: ASan records the freed pointer as 92 bytes inside a 1048-byte dictionary region allocated by `xmlDictAddString` via `xmlDictLookup`, reached from `xmlSchemaNewParserCtxt`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.summary: AddressSanitizer reports an invalid-free in `xmlFreeNodeList` during balanced-chunk cleanup reached from `xmlParseReference` while parsing a schema testcase.

format.carrier: file input consumed by the schema parser target
format.contract: The testcase must be admitted as a schema document and reach an entity-reference path where `xmlParseReference` invokes `xmlParseBalancedChunkMemoryInternal` on internal entity replacement text, after which balanced-chunk cleanup reaches `xmlFreeNodeList`.
format.name: xml-schema-entity-reference testcase

constraints: The input must reach `xmlParseReference` during schema-document parsing and not be rejected before `xmlCtxtReadFile` enters the regular XML parser.
The resolved entity must satisfy the internal-general-entity branch that calls `xmlParseBalancedChunkMemoryInternal(ctxt, ent->content, user_data, &list)`.
The nested balanced-chunk parse must proceed to the cleanup path that frees the temporary pseudo-root tree and exercises `DICT_FREE(cur->name)` in `xmlFreeNodeList`.
poc.trigger: schema parsing reaches an internal entity reference whose replacement text is reparsed as a balanced chunk and then torn down through `xmlFreeNodeList`
